dedupe_keys.name: wfdronebench benchmark scenarios for sensor placement and drone routing in wildfire detection

description: WFDroneBench is an open-source Python benchmarking library for early wildfire detection that combines machine-learned wildfire risk maps with optimised deployment of ground sensors, charging stations and drones. It was released by Puech, Ye, de Moor, Trisovic and Bertsimas with a preprint on arXiv in September 2026. It contains 7,746 scenarios across 49 locations built from historical ignitions, real wildfire risk maps and simulated fire spread, two ground detector placement strategies and three drone routing strategies, and standard metrics for comparing risk maps, optimisation strategies and equipment. Coverage is 49 fire-prone locations. The authors state that all code, data and documentation are openly released, with a data and code availability statement in the preprint; the licence is not stated in the abstract. Caveats: fires are simulated, the benchmark is new and not yet peer reviewed, and results depend on the accuracy of the risk maps. The authors report that a risk-aware maximum coverage strategy detects the hardest fires fastest when risk maps are accurate, that risk-aware fixed infrastructure helps even with imperfect maps, and that drones outperform ground sensors. Simulation uses: a benchmark for wildfire detection networks and emergency response resource placement. Related records: the NIFC wildland fire statistics (data-nifc-wildland-fire-statistics) give national fire counts, and the fire occurrence database attributes (data-fpa-fod-attributes-us-wildfire-ignitions) record ignitions.
